weakness: The pull was one open-loop linear move at constant speed. On a stiff drawer (damping 3000 N*s/m) the handle slid out of the pinch grasp after a few millimetres, the hand finished its motion empty, the API reported the motion as 'ok', and the pipeline believed it had pulled; all 3 retries repeated the same slip (travel ~0 on 10/10 seeds).
how_found: Questioned A1 (the articulated part moves freely and follows the hand). Real drawers stick and vary in stiffness, and the pipeline never compared where the hand went with where the drawer went.
why_missed: In the nominal scene the drawer follows the hand perfectly, so a successful motion status was taken as evidence that the object moved; no grasp check after closing and no progress check during the pull.
fix: Check gripper_holding() after closing (re-approach if empty); pull in 1 cm increments relative to the current hand pose (bounded force), after each increment check the grasp and the measured drawer travel (averaged detections), stop on slip or stall, then re-detect the handle and re-grasp from where the drawer now is (up to 4 attempts).
general_rule: When moving an object through contact, command small increments relative to the current measured pose and verify after each that the object itself moved and is still held; never infer object motion from the robot's own motion status.

weakness: The pipeline only planned around the scene: with a tall movable box standing where the hand must end up after the pull, every pre-grasp and pull step was refused as a collision (or the hand stopped on the force limit), on 10/10 seeds. It had no notion of the volume its own task motion needs, nor of rearranging movable clutter. During repair two more weaknesses appeared: a single-detection top grasp on a narrow object landed a finger on its rim and the object slipped out unnoticed, and the first 'free' spot chosen was in the forearm's sweep.
how_found: Questioned A6 (nothing stands in the volume swept by the hand and arm while approaching and pulling). Real drawers have things parked in front of them, and the pipeline's tilted-approach trick only avoids clutter that is low.
why_missed: In the nominal scene only low objects (plate) were near the drawer, and the planner's collision avoidance silently handled them, so the work volume was never made explicit.
fix: Before grasping the handle, compute the work volume (pull path plus palm/forearm margin) from the detected handle and pull direction; every non-cabinet obstacle that intrudes above handle height - 5 cm is picked (top grasp from 20-sample averaged detections) and placed on the nearest free table spot that is clear of other obstacles, of the work volume and of the base-to-hand forearm band; lifting is verified (object rose with the hand, still held) and the scene is re-checked after placing, with up to 3 tries.
general_rule: Before executing a contact motion, derive the full volume the robot will sweep (hand, palm and forearm, over the whole motion), and if a movable object intrudes, relocate it to a spot outside that volume and verify it moved, instead of hoping the planner finds a way around.

weakness: The work volume was checked for blockers exactly once, at the start. A box that slid into the space in front of the drawer one second later was never noticed: every pull step was refused as a collision and the retry loop just re-grasped the handle and tried the same blocked pull again (s_break 0.0). Repair exposed two more bugs: the work volume was recomputed from the current (partly opened) handle, so it drifted outward and swallowed every free table spot; and single noisy obstacle boxes flagged a low bowl as a blocker at random.
how_found: Questioned A8 (the scene is static after the first look). The pipeline cached the result of one perception pass and acted on it for the whole episode, and real workspaces change while the robot works (people put things down, objects slide).
why_missed: In all earlier scenes nothing moved on its own, so a single look was sufficient and the retry loop only ever retried the robot's own failure, not a changed scene.
fix: Every attempt now starts with fresh perception: re-detect the handle, re-check the work volume (computed from the closed-drawer reference = current handle minus measured travel), wait until blockers stop moving (averaged track windows), then clear them; a refused pull step ends the attempt so the next one re-perceives. Obstacle boxes are averaged over 8 calls before thresholding.
general_rule: Re-perceive before every attempt and every phase of a multi-step manipulation, derive safety volumes from fixed task references rather than from state that your own actions change, and treat a refused or blocked motion as a sign the scene changed, not as a reason to repeat the same motion.

weakness: The handle was only ever approached in the vertical plane of the pull axis (pitch varied, yaw never), so a fixed post standing just beyond the opened drawer front blocked the palm/forearm for every candidate approach. Worse, the clearing step tried to pick up the fixed post again and again (3 grasps per attempt, every attempt) and burned the whole 3000-step budget (10/10 seeds hit the step limit). Repair also showed the post-release retreat went along the pull direction, straight into the obstacle.
how_found: Questioned A4 (the space straight in front of and above the handle is free). The approach family had only one degree of freedom and the clutter-clearing step from round 2 silently assumed every obstacle is movable.
why_missed: Every earlier blocker was either low (avoided by pitching down) or movable (relocated), so the approach family and the 'clear it' strategy were never confronted with something that can be neither stepped over nor moved.
fix: Approach candidates now vary yaw (0, +-30, +-55 deg) as well as pitch; each candidate is scored by sampling fingers, palm (wide along the closing axis) and wrist at the current, half-open and fully-open grip poses against averaged obstacle boxes, and collision-free candidates are tried first. An obstacle that is held but does not rise when lifted is marked immovable and never re-grasped (it is planned around instead). After releasing the handle the hand retreats back along its own approach axis.
general_rule: When something is in the way, first test whether it can be moved (and remember the answer); for what cannot be moved, search over the full set of approach directions and check the whole hand-and-wrist sweep of the planned motion against it before committing, and always retreat along the direction you came in.

weakness: With the cabinet turned to face the robot (and moved), the drawer has to be pulled toward the robot base, so the hand's work volume now ran through the bowl, the wine bottle and next to the wine rack. The clearing step tried to top-grasp the 27 cm rack three times per attempt (force-limit hits), spent its tries on table spots the arm could not reach next to the rack, and the steep 35-45 deg approaches it fell back to drove the open upper finger into the drawer front; every seed ran out of steps (s_break 0.0). Repair also exposed that a bowl wider than the gripper can only be picked by its rim, and that a single failed grasp was being treated as 'immovable'.
how_found: Questioned A2/A3 (the cabinet stands where it usually does, facing sideways). A real robot meets furniture in other poses, and everything the pipeline derived (approach family, which clutter matters, where to put it) had only ever been exercised in one layout.
why_missed: In the nominal and earlier layouts the pull went sideways across open table, the only clutter in the work volume was a narrow box, and the 25-deg approach always worked first, so the gripper-geometry limits (opening width, finger reach past the handle standoff) and the reachability of placement spots were never tested.
fix: Approach candidates are scored by sampled hand/wrist collisions (fingers, palm, wrist out to 35 cm) and all are tried in order (refusals cost no time); tilts capped at 25 deg because the open finger must not reach past the handle standoff. Clearing: objects much wider than the gripper are not attempted; objects slightly wider are pinched at the rim nearest the robot; a refused placement switches to a spot at least 15 cm away (up to 4 spots); held-but-not-lifting marks immovable only for normal grasps; after one full failed clearing an object is remembered as immovable and planned around. The work-volume height threshold now reflects the palm's reach below the handle (8 cm).
general_rule: Before acting on an object, check the action's preconditions against the gripper's own geometry (opening width, finger length and reach) and the arm's reach, choose a grasp mode that fits (body, edge, or none), and bound the tries per object with memory of what failed, so a strategy tuned in one layout degrades into planning around rather than burning the time budget in another.
